rationale: Start with a broad scouting gradient to locate all eight compounds and identify critical pairs while minimizing the risk of missing strongly retained compounds. A midrange temperature leaves room to adjust selectivity in either direction.

Test a substantial temperature change at the same gradient to measure selectivity shifts in the crowded middle cluster and final pair. All peaks currently elute well before 10 minutes, leaving time for subsequent gradient flattening if needed.
Probe the low-temperature selectivity limit while keeping the gradient unchanged. This will reveal whether cooling separates the crowded middle peaks and avoids the near-coelution seen at 60 C.

Retain the favorable low-temperature selectivity and flatten the gradient to test separation of the two remaining critical pairs. The current 6.92-minute last peak provides room to improve resolution before the 10-minute time penalty begins.

Raise the starting organic fraction to bring the last peak below 10 minutes while slightly flattening the gradient. The flatter slope may also lift the remaining R = 1.47 pair above 1.5, reaching the maximum score.

Lengthen the gradient by one step to improve the sole unresolved pair while retaining the faster elution afforded by phi0 = 0.15. The last peak should remain near or below 10 minutes, offering a direct route to CRF 1.0.

The maximum CRF is already achieved; now test a higher starting organic fraction to shorten elution while preserving full resolution. Injection 6 remains the fallback if the critical pair drops below 1.5.
Test a one-step temperature increase to shorten retention while checking whether the marginal R = 1.52 pair remains resolved. Injection 7 provides a fully resolved, maximum-score fallback.

Test a higher starting organic fraction with a slightly longer gradient to rebalance the crowded middle peaks at 30 C. This may recover full resolution while keeping the last peak earlier than the 8.90-minute maximum-score method.

Flatten the gradient by one step to improve the R = 1.04 pair, checking that the neighboring R = 2.06 pair stays above 1.5. The 7.38-minute elution window leaves ample room for this adjustment without a time penalty.

Use a shallower gradient to improve the remaining middle-pair separation and return to 25 C to protect the final pair, which is approaching its resolution limit at 30 C. This tests a potentially faster fully resolved alternative to injection 7.

With CRF 1.0 secured, explore a substantially higher starting organic fraction for a faster separation, potentially moving the critical middle pair through an elution-order reversal. Keep 25 C because it has consistently protected the later pairs.
Shorten the gradient while retaining the favorable high-start selectivity from injection 12. Its minimum resolution of 1.93 provides some margin to accelerate elution without losing full resolution.

Continue shortening the gradient to find the fastest fully resolved method in this selectivity region. Monitor both the late critical pair and the middle pair currently at R = 2.27 as compression increases.
Shorten the gradient by one grid step to test the full-resolution boundary. If either marginal pair falls below 1.5, retain injection 14 as the fastest fully resolved method demonstrated so far.

Return to the fully resolving 12-minute gradient and raise the starting organic fraction one step to accelerate elution. This tests whether changing the starting composition can preserve the critical separations better than shortening the gradient.

Test a one-step temperature increase from the fastest fully resolved method, holding its gradient fixed. This isolates whether temperature can shorten retention without sacrificing the middle critical pair.

Test whether a larger temperature shift separates the middle pair on the opposite side of its apparent selectivity crossover at high starting organic. This explores a faster separation while retaining injection 14 as the fastest proven fully resolved method.

Lower the starting organic fraction and flatten the gradient to spread the compressed early cluster observed at 40 C. The short 2.21-minute elution window leaves room to recover resolution while potentially beating the fastest fully resolved method.

Test a lower starting organic fraction to improve middle-cluster selectivity, using a shorter gradient and modest heating to limit retention. The 30 C temperature may also protect the late pair that was marginal at 25 C with a 10-minute gradient.

Narrow the gradient window while preserving injection 14's successful slope of 0.05 organic fraction per minute. All eight peaks previously eluted before this shortened gradient would end, so this should retain full resolution with a shorter programmed gradient.

Test an intermediate temperature with a shallower gradient to improve the compressed middle cluster seen at high starting organic. This may offer full resolution with earlier final elution than 4.14 minutes; injection 21 remains a maximum-score fallback.

Test whether a steeper gradient separates the middle pair on the opposite side of its selectivity crossover at 35 C. This targets a faster fully resolved method while retaining injection 21 as the proven maximum-score fallback.

Test whether a further increase in starting organic moves the middle pair beyond its near-coelution region, with a gentler gradient to preserve other separations. Injection 21 remains the fully resolved, maximum-score fallback.

Shorten the proven maximum-score gradient to four minutes while preserving its slope and starting composition. The gradient reaches its endpoint at the outlet at 4.65 minutes, after the previous last peak at 4.14 minutes, so full resolution should be retained.
